details: On September 24-25, 2026, Iran proposed a seven-day plan to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and restart nuclear talks, contingent on the US lifting its naval blockade, waiving oil sanctions, and observing a ceasefire. Negotiations are ongoing in New York, but progress is reportedly stalled as neither side wants to concede leverage. The US had previously dismissed Iran's standing to make such an offer.
sourceName: Reuters (reported by Investing.com, FXStreet), The Independent, Al Jazeera
title: Iran Proposes Hormuz Reopening Amid US Talks, Stalled by Leverage Issues

details: On September 24, 2026, the latest US Purchasing Managers' Index (PMI) surged unexpectedly to 58.4, significantly exceeding market forecasts. This robust economic data intensified expectations for a Federal Reserve interest rate hike in October, with the probability now at nearly 70%. Consequently, the 10-year US Treasury yield jumped to 5.13%, its highest level since 2007.
title: US Business Activity Surges, Boosting Fed Rate Hike Expectations and Pressuring Crypto
